title: Simplify credential wrappers and async-generator surface for Py/TS/Go SDKs
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: tri-SDK ergonomics around streaming + auth have drifted: Python and TS expose slightly different async-generator ergonomics and Go uses a puller interface with inconsistent lifecycle signals. This PR simplifies credential wrapper shapes, clarifies retry semantics attached to credential refresh, and polishes the async-generator/pullstream surface so application authors have a consistent, minimal API across Python/TypeScript/Go. Changes are intentionally API-stable for most users; a small ergonomic rename in the Go iterator is called out below.

Summary of changes: - Introduce a lightweight CredentialWrapper abstraction (non-breaking) that standardizes token lookup + refresh hooks and an optional prefetch API used by streaming connectors. - Map credential retry presets to an explicit SDK-level RetryProfile enum so SDKs expose the same presets (fast-retry, steady, conservative). - Python: add an async generator adapter with consistent .aclose()/.__anext__() semantics and a convenience .resume(cursor) helper used by streaming examples. - TypeScript: normalize async iterator types to match the Python surface (AsyncGenerator<T, void, unknown>), and export RetryProfile and CredentialWrapper types in the top-level package index for ergonomic imports. - Go: add a small wrapper type PullIterator that implements io.Closer semantics and documents the rename from old StreamCursor -> PullCursor (compat shim included). - Tests/examples: update three quickstart examples (py/ts/go) to use the new shapes and add coverage for credential prefetch under jittered expiry.

Why this approach: SDKs previously relied on repo-specific helper shapes which caused surface mismatch in examples and led to subtle streaming edge cases on reauth + idempotent retries. The credential wrapper centralizes token TTL handling and exposes a concise prefetch hook that the runtime can call in advance without changing caller code. Making retry presets explicit prevents divergent presets across languages.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-2149) - [x] API surface proposal reviewed by SDK leads - [x] Unit tests added for each SDK - [x] Quickstart examples updated - [x] Docs snippet for migration and Go rename added

Compatibility notes: This PR is backwards-compatible for existing call sites in Python and TypeScript. Go sees a small ergonomic name change: StreamCursor -> PullIterator. A thin compat shim preserves the old type at runtime and logs a deprecation warning for one release. No runtime behavior changes expected beyond clearer lifecycle semantics (Close becomes recommended for long-lived streams).

Testing and CI: Initial CI run had a flaky test in python/streaming/test_reauth.py (timeout on CI worker). I re-ran the job after adding a 200ms jitter tolerance in the test harness (see commit 4) and the full pipeline passed. Local manual smoke tests: hand-tested cross-lang quickstarts against staging hosted API with long-lived streams and simulated token expiry.

Rollout plan: Merge to main and ship SDK minor bumps: python v0.19.0, typescript v1.27.0, go v1.8.0. Publish docs migration guide in docs/sdk/auth-migration.md and link from release notes. Monitor streaming error rates and credential refresh telemetry for two weeks.

Related: references ENG-2149, SDK-132; follows work on session-lease and retry-presets in previous PRs.
